query: Earlier studies of conventional metallic multilayers provide a general framework for deformation, but its conclusions may not transfer directly to high-entropy-alloy systems because compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order are associated with unusual deformation behavior. Preliminary evidence from FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers remains insufficient to establish what controls creep or when a given response dominates. Within the constraints of retaining a nanoscale multilayer coating and balancing strength with deformation tolerance, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading? State what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would expose it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, boundary conditions, relevant prior support, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: At intermediate homologous temperatures (≈0.3–0.5 Tm) the steady-state creep of nanoscale FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy (HEA) multilayer coatings is controlled by interface-dislocation-climb limited diffusion: solute-assisted pipe diffusion along the misfit-dislocation networks at semi-coherent interfaces supplies vacancies for dislocation climb, which in turn enables interfacial sliding and progressive plastic strain. The creep rate therefore scales with interface area (inverse bilayer period) and with the degree of solute segregation that lowers the activation barrier for pipe diffusion.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited 1 µm-thick HEA multilayer coating composed of equiatomic (CrMnFeCoNi) FCC layers alternated with (NbTiVTa) BCC layers; columnar grains, average bilayer period λ = 5 nm; no intentional dopants; interfaces semi-coherent with periodic misfit dislocation networks.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary bilayer period (λ = 2 nm, 10 nm, 50 nm) and independently add 2 at.% W to the BCC layers to suppress segregation at the interfaces.
generation.conditions: Constant uniaxial load giving 200 MPa applied stress (≈0.2 σy) at 600 °C (≈0.4 Tm, where Tm is the solidus of the average composition) for 100 h in high vacuum (<10-6 Torr).
generation.structural_mediator: Semi-coherent FCC/BCC interfaces containing periodic misfit dislocation arrays that act as one-dimensional fast-diffusion ‘pipes’.
generation.mechanism:
1. Applied stress generates an excess vacancy flux toward interface dislocation cores.
2. Solute enrichment (especially of low-diffusivity species) at the cores lowers the local activation energy for vacancy migration (chemical short-range order effect).
3. Accelerated pipe diffusion enables dislocation climb, permitting adjacent FCC and BCC layers to slide relative to one another.
4. The net plastic strain rate (steady-state creep) is therefore proportional to the areal density of such interfaces and to the efficacy of solute-assisted pipe diffusion.
generation.predicted_outcome:
• Fine multilayer (λ = 2 nm) will display a steady-state creep rate ε̇_ss ≈ 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹.
• Coarse multilayer (λ = 50 nm) will creep at least one order of magnitude more slowly (ε̇_ss ≤ 10⁻⁸ s⁻¹).
• Adding 2 at.% W to the fine multilayer will reduce ε̇_ss by ≥ 3× (to ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁸ s⁻¹) because W impedes segregation-assisted pipe diffusion.
• The apparent activation energy for creep will be ~60 % of the bulk lattice diffusion energy, consistent with interface (pipe) diffusion rather than bulk diffusion.
generation.baseline: Conventional Ni/Cu metallic multilayers of comparable λ tested under identical conditions creep at ≤ 10⁻⁹ s⁻¹, indicating that the HEA interfaces provide an additional, faster diffusion pathway.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis holds only for: (i) temperatures 0.25 Tm ≤ T ≤ 0.5 Tm, (ii) stresses below ~0.5–0.6 σy where dislocation glide becomes dominant, and (iii) bilayer periods ≤ 100 nm where interface area remains high. Outside these ranges, other creep mechanisms (bulk diffusion, grain-boundary diffusion, or glide-controlled power-law creep) should dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative creep rates may vary with exact composition and defect density; the extent to which W or other dopants suppress segregation is not yet known. The assumption of semi-coherent interfaces and uniform misfit-dislocation networks may not hold for all layer thicknesses.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three coating sets: (A) λ = 2 nm (undoped), (B) λ = 2 nm + 2 at.% W in BCC layers, (C) λ = 50 nm (undoped). Subject each to constant-load creep at 600 °C, 200 MPa for up to 100 h; repeat at 550 °C and 650 °C for activation energy determination. Post-mortem TEM and atom-probe tomography (APT) will characterize interface dislocation structures and segregation profiles.
measurements: Accumulated plastic strain vs time to derive ε̇_ss
Activation energy from temperature dependence of ε̇_ss
Interface chemistry by APT (solute segregation profiles)
Density and climb offsets of interface dislocations by TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if either (1) ε̇_ss does NOT decrease when λ is increased from 2 nm to 50 nm, (2) ε̇_ss for W-doped fine multilayers is not lower (within experimental error) than for undoped fine multilayers, or (3) activation energies match bulk lattice diffusion and TEM shows no evidence of dislocation climb at interfaces.
